source_observation.finding: _unique_observations enforces uniqueness only by observation_id, so multiple explicit observations may share one observation_key with conflicting values. evaluate_wake then evaluates EQUALS with any(item.value == expected_value), which can classify the condition as matched even when another explicit observation for the same key contradicts it.

hypothesis: Contradictory explicit observations for the same observation_key must not be collapsed into a positive wake match merely because one candidate equals the expected value. The evaluation should preserve conflict/unknown epistemics or require an explicit conflict-resolution policy before wake=true.
counterhypothesis: The intended semantics may be evidence-exists OR semantics where any explicit matching observation is sufficient even if another source disagrees. If that is intended, the contract must state this explicitly and bind source/authority/conflict policy because the current generic any-match rule otherwise erases disagreement.
